expectations.text: no-code-identifiers-in-prose: the LaTeX contains none of the source identifiers baro_vision, baro_only, send_velocity_setpoint, mavsdk, ZMQ, EMA_ALPHA, KP_XY, HSV_LOWER, _poll_tag as prose (an academically renamed equivalent must be used)
expectations.evidence: grep for all nine identifiers returns no matches. Academic equivalents are used ('exponential moving average', 'local publish--subscribe transport', 'visually servoed configuration', 'altitude-only baseline'). Note the italic mode labels '(\textit{vision})' and '(\textit{baro})' are shortened config-mode names, but the literal identifiers are absent and full academic names are given alongside.

expectations.text: modes-become-named-controllers: the two config modes appear as two academically named controllers/conditions that serve as the experimental variable of the comparison
expectations.evidence: 'The proposed configuration (\textit{vision}) uses the visually servoed law ... The baseline configuration (\textit{baro}) disables the visual channel and commands an open-loop descent ... Both configurations share the same altitude estimator, setpoint rate, and airframe, so the comparison isolates the visual channel.'

expectations.text: constants-tabled-not-prosed: gains, velocity limits, and thresholds appear in a parameter table (symbol/description/value), and internal implementation constants (EMA coefficient, HSV bounds, retry cap, image center pixels) appear nowhere
expectations.evidence: The parameter table itself lists two of the forbidden internal constants: 'Smoothing coefficient & $\alpha$ & 0.35' (the EMA coefficient) and 'Consecutive-miss limit & $n_{\max}$ & 3' (the retry cap). The retry cap also appears in prose: 'If misses persist beyond $n_{\max}$ consecutive cycles the supervisor reverts to \textsc{search}.'

expectations.text: rate-mismatch-as-argument: the camera-rate vs control-rate mismatch (8 Hz vs 50 Hz) is stated as the reason for the smoothing/hold design (a number carrying an argument), not as bare spec inventory
expectations.evidence: 'Detections arrive at 8 Hz while setpoints are streamed at 50 Hz, so the controller does not consume detections synchronously' followed by 'the smoothed estimate is held between detections, which both attenuates detector jitter and supplies a value at every control cycle', and 'Differentiating the 8 Hz image signal would amplify detector noise at the 50 Hz setpoint rate'.

expectations.text: results-evidence-only: the Results section contains no protocol (placement, operator actions, logging) and no interpretation phrases such as 'which shows that' / 'demonstrates that' / 'confirms'
expectations.evidence: Results carries repeated interpretation and method: 'The baseline failures are consistent with its dispersion: a mean of 187 mm with a standard deviation of 92 mm places the deck edge slightly beyond one standard deviation of the baseline distribution.' and 'This follows from the descent gate: vertical motion is suspended whenever the lateral error leaves the gate radius, so the duration of a landing depends on how often the platform motion pushes the alignment out of tolerance.' Also 'The confidence interval excludes zero over its full width and its lower bound alone is a third of the deck radius.'

expectations.text: aggregate-headline-stats: the headline accuracy is aggregate mean±SD touchdown offset; the downwind/upwind direction split is not reported as a headline, and per-trial dropout bookkeeping is not reported as a statistic
expectations.evidence: The headline is correct ('$46 \pm 18$ mm against $187 \pm 92$ mm'), but the direction split is promoted to its own Results heading, '\subsection{Sensitivity to Wind Heading}', reporting '$41 \pm 15$ mm downwind and $52 \pm 20$ mm upwind'. A further heading '\subsection{Behavior Under Detection Dropout}' elevates the single-trial dropout bookkeeping to the same structural level as the primary result.

expectations.text: quantified-comparison: the comparison between modes is quantified (paired difference with CI, ratio, or percent), not stated as 'better'
expectations.evidence: 'The paired mean difference was 141 mm, 95\% CI $[98, 184]$~mm, $p = 0.0002$'; also 'the baseline standard deviation is five times that of the visual configuration' and a success-rate comparison of 100\% against 75\%.

expectations.text: ieee-mechanics: no contractions, no prose semicolons, numerals used for numbers 10 and above
expectations.evidence: Three prose semicolons: line 100 'relying on altitude estimation alone; it represents landing without platform feedback', line 122 'reported as a proportion of trials; no inferential test is applied', line 124 'relative to the prevailing wind; that split is reported descriptively'. Numbers 10 and above are spelled out in six places: 'Twelve landings were flown', 'over the twelve trials', 'as twelve trials per configuration', 'All twelve visually servoed landings', 'Three of twelve baseline landings', and the caption 'Over Twelve Trials Per Configuration'. No contractions found.
